main_text.l: CAPUT I. De corporis naturalis definitione, & materia prima.
Hactenus proœmium scientiæ Physicæ: sequitur ipsa tractatio: cuius pars generalis corpus naturale definit, eiusque principia & affectiones pertractat.
Corpus naturale est substantia materiâ & formâ proprie sic dictis constans.

Materia & Forma, si in propria & Philosophica significatione accipiantur, sunt duæ substantiæ imperfectæ & incompletæ, quæ conjunctæ substantiam perfectam, & completam sensibilem constituunt, quæ corpus appellatur, vel substantia corporea, & contradistinguitur substantiæ Spirituali

page.notes: The text runs to the foot of the page, so the last line is complete. The large initial H of "Hactenus" is joined to the word. The Greek heading "Ἐξήγησις" is set in a stylised form and is transcribed as the standard word.
